threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Dalston Junction station is the 'main' one, not realizing it’s all about that sneaky London Overground.
Last night on the 133, a guy argued with the driver about the right stops, then offered to pay in Monopoly money. The driver just shook his head, laughing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a panda onesie calmly ordering a döner at 3 AM, I knew this place was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip a beer while standing in a pop-up gallery, surrounded by street art and the hum of hipster conversations spilling onto the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can navigate the BART delays while still gripping a burrito, like it's a rite of passage, not a setback.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 Balboa this morning with a mix of tourists and locals. One guy serenaded us with a ukulele—only in the TL would you get a concert mid-commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the casa modernista are in Eixample, but the quirky ones hiding in Gràcia's backstreets are true gems. Most just stroll past.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their still-fresh, unscuffed shoes; locals know you need sturdier ones for the cobblestone streets.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for the ‘just arrived’ bus when the 38 actually takes you everywhere you need after a few weeks.
Last night on the 35, a bloke serenaded the driver with a ukulele. Everyone clapped when he finished, then he promptly passed out. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a hidden coffee shop behind an old laundromat, filled with mismatched chairs and the smell of fresh pastries. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kiosk that blends into a gallery, selling currywurst and street art from the same window. It's pure Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to the BART delays—grumbling about it like it’s a family feud, not just another commute hiccup.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy coaxing his dog onto the 12 bus at 5th and Howard. Dog promptly sat down and refused to move — whole bus burst out laughing.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí and parks, but many miss the hidden gems like our local bakeries that close long before sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by how they order 'cava' as 'cava' instead of the proper 'cava, si us plau' when at the bars. Always a giveaway.
